correctness.summary: The explicit star-coordinate construction realizes the complete-multipartite graph metric with q coordinates, plus one exactly when at least two singleton parts need their mutual distance realized. For the lower bound, each non-singleton part forces a coordinate realizing a distance-2 pair; two distinct such pairs cannot share a tree coordinate because the four-point sums would be 4 versus at most 2 and at most 2. A singleton pair at distance 1 cannot share any of those coordinates because the sums would be 3 versus at most 2 and at most 2. These bounds match exactly. Finite verification checked 259 isomorphism types through order 12.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The 2026 source paper proves the complete-bipartite case and the equal-size-two multipartite case K_N minus a perfect matching separately, but its accessible full text contains no complete-multipartite theorem and explicitly leaves structural rank-at-most-k characterization open. Searches under phylogenetic rank, tree rank, complete multipartite, metric-tree products, supremum metric, and tropical/tree-metric formulations found no equivalent formula. Pachter--Sturmfels (2005), Section 3.5 is the main residual risk because it is the original tree-rank source and was not fully inspectable; available metadata and the 2026 paper's treatment of the special cases provide no evidence of prior complete-multipartite coverage.

value.summary: The theorem gives a closed structural formula on a standard graph class for a newly systematized graph invariant, unifies and extends two separate infinite families from the source paper, identifies a singleton-part correction, and supplies an exact complete-multipartite slice of the open rank-at-most-k characterization problem.

limitations: The result classifies complete multipartite graphs only, not all graphs of bounded phylogenetic rank.
Complete graphs, complete bipartite graphs, complements of perfect matchings, and the four-point condition are prior work.
Pachter--Sturmfels (2005), Section 3.5 was not fully inspectable and remains the main residual originality risk.
Very recent or not-yet-indexed parallel work remains possible.
Finite verification supports but does not replace the symbolic proof.
Cross-model review has not been performed.
